transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-10 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Dr. Priya Rao (Sierra Biotech Head of ML), Tom Ellis (Platform Eng), Nina Park (Security Lead), Samuel Ortega (CTO)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, rough): Handoff from AE to CSM and SE. Confirmed pilot scope (ingest pipelines, embedding store, LLM chat endpoint for internal R&D). Security questions around VPC peering, KMS, and audit logs. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with performance targets and a follow-up check on 2025-07-24.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Avery from Redwood, I'll run quick through agenda — handoff to Lina for CS, Marcus will cover the runbook and benchmark steps.
[00:32] Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks, Avery. Quick intros — I'm Priya, I lead ML at Sierra. We're excited to get Redwood set up; main goals are low latency for our inference calls and data controls, altho- uh, a lot of legal constraints.
[00:50] Samuel Ortega: Samuel here — CTO — high level, we need private deploy on VPC, and also proof that logs and keys never leave our tenancy.
[01:10] Lina Gomez: Hi! Lina, Customer Success. I'll be your main touchpoint for the rollout. My plan is to map milestones, owners, and coordinate with Marcus on the technical steps.
[01:30] Marcus Patel: Hey all. I'll speak to the benchmarking steps. We typically ask for a traffic sample, a few representative prompts, and a few infra details — e.g., average sequence length, typical concurrency, and KV cash patterns — excuse me, KV cache — that you expect.
[01:55] Tom Ellis: On concurrency, we're seeing 20-40 concurrent requests for our dev model but plan 200 concurrent for prod. Latencies need to be under 200ms P50 for chat-ish flows.
[02:20] Nina Park: Security-wise, we want to validate KMS integration, audit logs, SSO/SAML with Okta, and retention controls. Also SOC 2 type II — do you have the certs?
[02:40] Avery Chen: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 docs. We also have an enclave-like option for private deployments and HSM integrations via KMS providers — we'll include that in the security pack.
[03:05] Dr. Priya Rao: For the pilot, success metrics are: P50 <200ms, P95 <500ms, 2% or less token-level quality regressions vs baseline, and cost per 1k tokens under X (we'll give a target).
[03:35] Marcus Patel: Great. Practically for the 2-week pilot we propose: week 0 prep (config + access), week 1 run baseline tests and run synthetic traffic, week 2 run live traffic with A/B routing to fallback model. We'll capture token counts and lat distributions.
[04:05] (cross talk)
[04:15] Tom Ellis: For networking — do you require peering or can you do private endpoint? We prefer not to open wide peering.
[04:32] Marcus Patel: Both options exist — private endpoint + private control plane. For some regulated customers we do VPC peering, others prefer managed private endpoints; I'll follow up with docs.
[05:00] Speaker 1: there's also the cost question — reserved capacity versus on-demand —how does that look?
[05:10] Avery Chen: We discussed reserved capacity earlier in sales — for predictability/resourcing we can propose Dedicated GPU pools. For short pilots, hosted with caps is easiest. We'll include both price comparisons.
[05:35] Dr. Priya Rao: On data residency, all data needs to stay in the us-west-2 region for now. Are there any automated fallback routes that could route traffic outside region?
[05:55] Marcus Patel: Routing policies can be pinned to region; fallback is configurable, we can turn off cross-region fallback to meet residency requirements.
[06:20] Nina Park: Auditability — we need token-level traceability (not payload storage but metadata) and long retention on logs for 1 year. Any issues with that?
[06:40] Lina Gomez: We'll map log retention options. There's an add-on for extended retention; I'll add pricing.
[06:55] Samuel Ortega: Ok, good. I want to make sure we have a clear owner list.
[07:10] Avery Chen: Sure — for Redwood: Avery (commercial), Marcus (SE/benchmarks), Lina (CS lead). For Sierra: Priya (ML owner), Tom (platform), Nina (security), Samuel (exec sponsor).
[07:30] Dr. Priya Rao: Two quick technical clarifications: (1) how do you handle KV cache warm starts across model restarts? (2) is quantized model support available for our workload?
[07:50] Marcus Patel: KV cache persists across sessions only if you enable prefix caching and route through the same shard; warms are handled automatically if you bind sessions. Quantization: yes we support int8 and hybrid routes; we'll recommend a quantization profile after sample runs. It does impact quality slightly — we'll measure with the evals.
[08:20] Tom Ellis: Regarding embeddings — we plan to use embeddings for semantic search. Do you recommend vector DB integration or built-in caching?
[08:38] Marcus Patel: We integrate with common vector DBs and also provide an embeddings cache. For high QPS, a DB like Pinecone or our recommended vector store is better. We'll share a pattern doc.
[08:55] Speaker 2: Are there DR/backups for the model artifacts?
[09:05] Marcus Patel: Model artifacts are versioned in S3 and we have multi-zone replication for Dedicated plans; for Private on-prem we'll discuss local storage strategies.
[09:30] (brief hold as folks check links)
[10:00] Lina Gomez: To be conservative on timeline, we suggest this onboarding cadence: Day 0-3: access and accounts + security review; Day 4-10: bench runs + config; Day 11-14: live pilot and acceptance. Looking at target dates, that puts acceptance around 2025-07-24 if we start next week.
[10:35] Dr. Priya Rao: That timing is fine. We'll need a runbook though — can Marcus outline sample tests?
[10:50] Marcus Patel: Sure — sample tests: single-client latency sweep with 1-500 tokens, concurrency stress up to 250 conns, batch size variation, and key-value cache hit/miss scenarios. I'll produce a spreadsheet with exact test cases.
[11:15] Tom Ellis: For authentication, we use Okta and mTLS for internal services. Does Redwood support mTLS?
[11:30] Avery Chen: mTLS is supported on Dedicated/Private. For hosted we support Okta SAML + private endpoints; we'll outline options.
[12:00] Nina Park: On encryption, keys must be customer-managed; can you integrate with our Azure Key Vault?
[12:15] Marcus Patel: We support KMS providers — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations. Azure Key Vault is on our roadmap; I'll flag that as an item and give you an interim solution.
[12:40] (audio glitch)
[13:00] Dr. Priya Rao: For the quality metrics, we'll send two golden prompt sets and expected outputs. We want Redwood to run regressions and alert on >2% divergence.
[13:20] Lina Gomez: We have quality monitoring and regression alerts in Redwood Optimize, we'll configure threshold alerts and link them to the pilot dashboard.
[13:40] Speaker 3: Can we get a burn-rate estimate for expected traffic?
[13:55] Avery Chen: We'll calculate based on sample token counts and concurrency. We'll include both hosted and dedicated cost projections in the pricing packet.
[14:20] (long pause while someone pulls docs)
[14:50] Marcus Patel: I'll also include a short note on quantization tradeoffs — sample numbers from similar customers.
[15:10] Samuel Ortega: One governance ask — is there a way to restrict model classes (no web-browsing or external tool calls) from the runtime?
[15:28] Marcus Patel: Yes, we have policy controls and can disable function/tool-calls and streaming/ external connectors at the deployment level. We'll show the policy UI screenshot.
[15:50] Dr. Priya Rao: Ok thanks.
[16:05] Avery Chen: Quick recap of action items then next steps: we'll send SOC 2, onboarding checklist, pricing packet, and Marcus will send the benchmark spreadsheet. Lina will schedule a follow-up check on 2025-07-24 at same time.
[16:30] Tom Ellis: For access, who should we provision in Redwood — just the three of us? We'll need dev and prod roles.
[16:45] Lina Gomez: Yes please share an IAM list, and I'll set up project-level roles (viewer, operator, admin).
[17:00] Dr. Priya Rao: We'll send sample prompts by Friday (7/17).
[17:10] Avery Chen: Great. Anything else?
[17:20] Nina Park: One final — please include a copy of the audit log schema so our engineers can parse it.
[17:30] Marcus Patel: Will do.
[17:45] (meeting closing pleasantries)
[18:00] Avery Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and Lina will own the schedule.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-words (KV cash), speaker tag flips for a few lines, timestamps are approximate.

Recap / Agreed Milestones (verbatim):
- 2025-07-12: Redwood to send onboarding checklist, SOC 2, pricing packet (Avery)
- 2025-07-16: Sierra to share security control list & audit schema (Nina)
- 2025-07-17: Sierra to share sample prompts and traffic sample (Priya)
- 2025-07-18: Marcus to share benchmark spreadsheet results plan
- 2025-07-24: Follow-up check-in and pilot acceptance review (Lina to schedule)

End of transcript.
